ui.cm_title: What NASA already documents as countermeasures — reference, not a prescription
ui.cm_intro: C-Sync does not choose, dose or schedule any countermeasure. It points to the onboard procedure and leaves the decision to the crew medical officer and the flight surgeon. The rows below are what NASA publishes, with the source.

cm_rows.nasa: On the International Space Station, exercise with a treadmill, a cycle ergometer and a resistive device is used to protect muscle strength, aerobic fitness, bone density and sensorimotor performance. NASA is now testing whether a treadmill is still needed (study in progress, no results yet).
cm_rows.csync: Does not measure exercise. No recommendation.

cm_rows.nasa: NASA lists sleep loss, circadian desynchronization and work overload as a risk. An in-flight lighting schedule exists on the Station for circadian adaptation. NASA states that validated, individualised countermeasures are still a research gap.
cm_rows.csync: Reported sleep (PH09) below the personal baseline for 2 days opens procedure PROC-FATIGUE-01 and refers to the crew medical officer.
cm_rows.source: NASA Human Research Roadmap, risk 100; gap Sleep-102; task 1453

ui.hook_title: Kora Mensah has chest pain. Earth cannot hear her.
ui.hook_text: Flight engineer. She reported it at 14:10. The link to Earth is down from 13:00 to 19:00, so her report reaches the ground at 19:20. Who decides in the meantime, and on what? Two days earlier, her sleep and reaction time had already started to worsen.
ui.hook_tl_gap: {h} h {m} min before the report reaches Earth
ui.beat1_line: C-Sync is learning what normal looks like for Kora. Days 1 to 5 are her own reference.
ui.beat2_line: Short sleep two nights in a row, slower reactions. Not her usual. She says she is just tired.
ui.beat3_line: A symptom is reported. A guided checklist opens. C-Sync never names what is wrong; the commander or the medical officer decides.
ui.beat4_line: No link from 13:00 to 19:00. The report is saved on board and reaches the ground once, at 19:20.
ui.beat5_line: Day 10. Kora asks to go back to work. Her last heart-rate reading is 14 minutes old and the limit is 10, so C-Sync does not clear her until it is measured again.
ui.beat6_line: A simulated crew and a rule tuned on simulated scenarios, with no clinical validation. Next: expert review, analog data, real sensors.
ui.why_title: Why compare a person with their own normal?
ui.why_intro: Fixed published limits (sleep under 7 h, 11 or more reaction-time lapses) ignore that people differ. In 150 simulated crews per row, each cell shows how often the rule opens a procedure on a crew whose condition worsens / on a healthy crew. The personal rule uses the same two signals as the fixed one. A single fixed limit catches every drift, but it also wrongly opens procedures on healthy crews.
ui.why_limits: SIMULATED. The spread between people is an invented setting, not a measurement. The data generator and the rule were designed together, so this shows a sensitivity, not a proof. Fixed limits come from other settings (sleep societies, airport screening).
ui.ref_title: What if the days taken as normal were already off?
ui.ref_intro: Not in this demo yet: a pre-mission reference recorded on Earth. The personal rule needs its first five days to be normal. If the crew is already tired, it measures against a false normal. Each cell: drifts caught / healthy crews wrongly flagged. The cross-check swaps in the Earth reference when it is clearly better than the first five days.
ui.ref_cost: The cost: if life in space really differs from life on Earth, the cross-check wrongly flags {a5} % of healthy crews when the gap is small and {a1} % when it is large. The real gap is unknown, so these two numbers are stress tests, not measurements.
ui.why_synth: SIMULATED crews. Source: research/fixed_vs_personal.py and research/hybrid_baseline.py.

ui.scale_title: Evidence at scale: computed now, not typed in
ui.scale_real_h: 1. Real NASA telemetry, re-processed from the raw file
ui.scale_real_intro: Raw file from the NASA OSDR Environmental Data App (SHA-256 checked). Quality control runs on every 5-minute point: a flat run of one hour or more is flagged ARTIFACT, never read as normal. Habitat state from cabin CO2 only: no crew physiology, nothing clinical.
ui.scale_usable: {n} missions have usable ISS CO2 and are listed. Reprocessed in {s} s.
ui.scale_crews_h: 2. Synthetic crews through the same rule, on fresh seeds
ui.scale_crews_intro: Rule v3 as shipped (d ≥ 1.5 on 2 days in a row), no retuning. Seeds from {s0} are used nowhere else. A fresh run can differ from the published figure: the interval is the honest range. Synthetic crews built by our own generator, not astronauts.
ui.scale_healthy: Healthy crew (a procedure here is a false one)
ui.sbar_s_t: Day 7 check-in compared with the personal baseline of days 1–5 (synthetic crew member).
ui.sbar_b_t: Baseline built from days 1–5. Rule v3: flagged at d ≥ 1.5 on 2 consecutive days. A missing value reads UNKNOWN.
ui.sbar_r_cont: No procedure proposed. A human decides.
ui.next_title: After the pitch — planned, not done yet
ui.next_intro: These are next steps for the team. None of them is part of what the prototype does today.
next_items: Review of the rules by space-medicine experts (the medical review is still pending).
Trial on simulated-isolation mission data, the nearest real data we know of.
Adapters for real sensors, so measured values replace the guided entry.
A pre-mission baseline, because a crew member who is tired during days 1–5 skews the reference.
Protection of health data: encryption and access control. Nothing is in place yet.
A printed-procedure backup for a power loss.
Cost of integration: not estimated yet, so no figure is given.
ui.cmd_title: Commander board — six synthetic crew members
ui.cmd_intro: The same rule v3 runs on each member against their own baseline. The board only sorts, most urgent first. It decides nothing: every open procedure waits for a human decision.
ui.cmd_summary: Day {day}: {n_open} procedure(s) open, {n_deg} degraded, {n_watch} watch, {n_unk} unknown.
ui.cmd_note: A single flag (Watch) is not an alert: one indicator left its baseline. Crew F has a simulated sensor gap from day 6, so its Body state reads Unknown, never Normal. Days 1–5 are the baseline: every state is Unknown.
ui.cmd_synth: SYNTHETIC DATA — six invented crew members (seeds 61001–61006), not real astronauts.
